title: Can KV Cache Be Reused Across Model Updates? A DeepSeek-V4-Flash Case Study
summary: The technique replaces recomputing KV caches for shared long prefixes after a model weight update by directly reusing the previous version's cache. It costs nothing in new computation at reuse time, but introduces divergence between reused-cache and native inference behavior, which grows with prefix length in single-token retrieval tasks. It can fail through large retrieval-accuracy losses on some updates and through disagreement in answer content or stopping behavior even when the first generated token matches.
rationale: The TTFT gain is real and cheap to exploit on constrained infrastructure, but retrieval accuracy varies from near-native to large losses across updates, so adoption requires per-model, per-workload validation of task utility and behavioral fidelity before production use.

claims.statement: The technique replaces recomputing KV caches for shared long prefixes after a model weight update by directly reusing the previous version's cache. It costs nothing in new computation at reuse time, but introduces divergence between reused-cache and native inference behavior, which grows with prefix length in single-token retrieval tasks. It can fail through large retrieval-accuracy losses on some updates and through disagreement in answer content or stopping behavior even when the first generated token matches.
With source caches already available, direct reuse across model updates achieves median time-to-first-token speedups of 2.10–5.08x on three longer-prefix QA benchmarks.
